product.name: Sandbox
promise: The rest of the host, absent.
product.lede: b10x-sandbox respawns your shell, or one command, inside a bubblewrap sandbox. The current directory is writable at /workspace, the directories you name with --dir are mirrored beside it, toolchain homes can be added read-only with --ro, and nothing else from the host is visible apart from /usr, /bin, /lib and /lib64. No network unless --net. It is a wrapper with Substrate's namespace and mount posture, not a daemon.
product.meta: Rust library and CLI · Linux · bubblewrap or Docker · Apache-2.0

sections.title: Name what the process may see.
sections.lede: Every host directory enters the sandbox through --dir or --ro, and every other path is simply not mounted. A path that does not fit is refused by name, never adjusted.

items.title: Substrate's isolation set
items.description: Own user, ipc, pid, uts and net namespaces, no nested user namespace, private /proc /dev /tmp, a cleared environment, and death with the parent.

items.title: A mirrored workspace
items.description: With --dir, the common ancestor becomes /workspace and each directory sits at its relative path, so ../lib resolves exactly as on the host.

items.title: Refusal, never fallback
items.description: No bwrap or no docker exits 2 with the program's name. Nothing runs unconfined, and nothing silently switches backend.

items.title: Bubblewrap or Docker
items.description: Bubblewrap is the default; --backend docker runs the same layout as your uid with no capabilities and a read-only image root.

sections.title: Early. Here is exactly what exists.
sections.lede: Shipped means code on main, held by a named test. Nothing is released yet: build from source.

tools.name: Substrate
tools.description: The governed execution service whose bubblewrap namespace and mount set this tool copies; it adds what this does not have: cgroup bounds, quotas, a seccomp filter and a durable operation record.
